floor.sink.foot.rationale: The outsole and heel cushioning of an ordinary shoe compress by a few millimetres under body weight, and the eye accepts that much. G-4's existing bound, kept.
floor.sink.foot.source: step-26 G-4 (standard.py SOLE_TOL_M = 0.005); a footwear compression reference was not read in S36-P1

floor.sink.shin.rationale: A trouser hem may brush the floor; the same bound as the sole.

floor.float.planted.rationale: A planted foot must read as planted. In normal walking the swinging foot clears the floor by only about 13 mm at its lowest (minimum toe clearance), so a planted foot floating more than that looks like a swinging one; the bound sits below it (Q-S36-3).
floor.float.planted.source: D. A. Winter, 'Foot trajectory in human gait: a precise and multifactorial motor control task', Physical Therapy 72(1):45-53, 1992. Citation confirmed; the ~1.3 cm figure was read only second-hand (S. B. Taylor, PhD thesis, Victoria University, attributing it to Winter); P2 confirms it from the paper

floor.float.walk_frame.rationale: In a walk one foot is always on the floor; the lowest point of each frame may float at most this far.
floor.float.walk_frame.source: S26-c-ground probe and scripts/check_cast.py CC-9 (float 20 mm)

self.limb_in_trunk.rationale: An arm resting against the flank compresses skin and fat by a few millimetres; deeper is a visible clip. G-9's bound, kept.

self.hand_in_trunk.rationale: The same reason as the limb, for the hand on the hip or the belly.

garment.poke.body.rationale: About the thickness of the cloth itself: woven shirting is under 0.5 mm, denim under 1 mm, knitwear 1-3 mm.
garment.poke.body.source: step-32 §7.2 W-4 (pose_sheet.gd POKE_MM = 2). ASTM D1777 is the thickness test method; its scope was read and it states no per-fabric figures, so the figures above remain uncited

garment.poke.layer.rationale: An inner layer poking through an outer one; the same cloth-thickness reason as garment.poke.body.
garment.poke.layer.source: step-36 §3.3, the same basis as garment.poke.body (W-4)

item.rest.floor.rationale: A floor-standing prop that floats or sinks by more shows a seam or loses its contact shadow at a 2 m viewing distance.
item.rest.floor.source: step-36 §3.3 plausibility; no viewing-distance test was run in S36-P1

item.overlap.parts.rationale: Rigid parts do not interpenetrate in reality; 2 mm covers tessellation error.

scene.mesh_over_solid.rationale: The server keeps a person's centre 250 mm (PERSON_RADIUS) from a solid; half a man's shoulder breadth is about 200 mm (biacromial breadth about 400 mm); 250 - 200 - 10 (GAP) is about 40 mm, the overhang a shoulder never meets.
scene.mesh_over_solid.source: ANSUR II (US Army, 2012) biacromial breadth, not read in S36-P1; P5 confirms the percentile
